title: News feed / Twitter timeline (fan-out)
relevance: High — canonical "design Twitter / Instagram / Facebook News Feed" HLD round at FAANG, Meta PA, and Indian product cos (Flipkart, Uber, Atlassian, etc.); the celebrity / hybrid fan-out tradeoff is the probe that separates mid from senior.
company_notes: Campus/new-grad: extremely common as Design Twitter/Instagram/News Feed; expected signal is hybrid fan-out + Redis ID timelines + async workers. Experienced/Meta PA/mid-level: same prompt with deeper probes on celebrity threshold, reconstruction, delete/fan-in, ranking candidates, multi-DC, graph hotspots. Among the top 5 product HLD questions; sister prompts are notification fan-out and design Facebook News Feed.

phases.goal: Scope post, follow, home vs user timeline, NFRs, and explicit cuts before designing.

must_hit.point: Functional scope covers post tweet (text; optional media URL), uni-directional follow/unfollow, reverse-chronological paginated home timeline from followees, and user timeline by one author.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate lists post, follow/unfollow, home feed, and profile/user timeline, and says home is the hard fan-out problem.

must_hit.point: Prefer high availability over strong consistency for feed freshness; eventual consistency for a few seconds is acceptable.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate states feeds can lag briefly and HA/freshness beats strict consistency on the read path.

must_hit.point: Home timeline p99 latency target is ~100–200 ms after hydrate.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate names a ~100–200 ms p99 read target after hydration, not just 'fast reads'.

must_hit.point: Explicitly cut full-text search, Trends, DMs, and algorithmic For You unless the interviewer pulls them in.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate parks search/Trends/DMs/For You and keeps the whiteboard on post + follow + home timeline.

probes: What are in-scope functional requirements, and what do you explicitly leave out?
What consistency and latency goals would you state for the home timeline?

hints.1: Start with post, follow, and the two timeline types users actually see.
hints.2: Separate home (merge of followees) from user timeline (one author), then name HA vs consistency.
hints.3: Scope: post + follow + reverse-chrono home + user timeline; eventual OK for a few seconds; p99 ~100–200 ms after hydrate; cut search/Trends/DMs/For You.

phases.goal: Use DAU, write/read QPS, and follower power-law to justify hybrid fan-out and ID-only Redis homes.

must_hit.point: Example write load: 200M DAU, avg 2 tweets/user/day → ~400M tweets/day ≈ ~5K writes/s avg (10–20K peak).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate walks 200M DAU × ~2 tweets/day to ~400M/day and ~5K writes/s avg with 10–20K peak.

must_hit.point: Timeline reads dominate: each user opens feed ~10×/day → ~20B reads/day ≈ ~200K+ QPS avg; read:write is often ~50:1+.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate shows ~10 opens/day → ~20B reads/day / ~200K+ QPS and calls the product read-heavy (~50:1+).

must_hit.point: Avg ~200 followers but celebrity outliers at 10M–100M make pure push write amplification the cliff.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate contrasts ~200 average followers with 10M–100M celebrities and says pure push blows up writes.

must_hit.point: Home cache ~800 IDs × 16–24 B ≈ ~15–20 KB/user; active users imply multi-TB Redis RAM, so store IDs only.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate sizes ~800 × 16–24 B ≈ ~15–20 KB/user and concludes ID-only timelines to keep RAM feasible.

probes: Walk a back-of-envelope for tweet write QPS and home-timeline read QPS.
Why does pure fan-out-on-write fail at celebrity scale, and what does that imply for the home cache?

hints.1: Pick round DAU and tweets-per-user, then estimate feed opens per day.
hints.2: Contrast average followers with celebrity outliers, then size Redis home entries.
hints.3: 200M DAU → ~5K writes/s avg; ~10 opens/day → ~200K+ QPS reads; celebrities 10M–100M; ~800 IDs ≈ ~15–20 KB/user → hybrid + ID-only Redis.

phases.goal: Define REST surfaces for tweets, follows, and cursored home/user timelines with auth-safe identity.

must_hit.point: Expose tweet CRUD-ish APIs (POST/GET/DELETE /v1/tweets), follow APIs (POST /v1/follows, DELETE /v1/follows/{followee_id}), GET user timeline, and GET /v1/feed for home.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate sketches tweet, follow, /users/{id}/tweets, and /feed endpoints matching the product verbs.

must_hit.point: Auth comes from the token; never trust user_id in the body for 'me'.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate says the authenticated principal is taken from the token, not a client-supplied user_id for self actions.

must_hit.point: Pagination cursor is last tweet_id (Snowflake) or timestamp — not fragile offsets.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate rejects OFFSET and uses a Snowflake tweet_id or time cursor for pages.

probes: Sketch the REST APIs for posting, following, and reading home vs user timelines.
How do you paginate the feed safely under concurrent inserts?

hints.1: List the write and read endpoints users need for tweets and follows.
hints.2: Call out auth-from-token and cursor vs offset.
hints.3: POST/GET/DELETE tweets; POST/DELETE follows; GET /users/{id}/tweets and GET /feed with cursor=last tweet_id/time; identity from token only.

phases.goal: Place tweets, dual-indexed follow graph, ID-only home cache, and hydration object caches.

must_hit.point: Tweet store: tweet_id PK, author_id, text, media refs, created_at; shard by tweet_id or author_id for user-timeline locality.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate models tweets with those fields and mentions sharding by tweet_id or author_id.

must_hit.point: Follow graph stores edges (follower_id → followee_id) plus a reverse index: fan-out needs followers-of(author); feed merge needs followees-of(me).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate requires both directions of the social graph for write fan-out and read-side celebrity merge.

must_hit.point: Home timeline cache is Redis list/ZSET home:{user_id} of tweet IDs, capped ~800, trimmed with LTRIM/ZREMRANGEBYRANK.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate puts only IDs in Redis homes, caps ~800, and names trim/remrange maintenance.

must_hit.point: Separate tweet:{id} and user:{id} object caches (plus CDN for media) hydrate after ID fetch.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate keeps timeline cache ID-only and hydrates tweet/user objects from caches/DB/CDN.

probes: What entities and stores do you need for tweets, follows, and home timelines?
Why not put full tweet text in every follower's home timeline entry?

hints.1: Name Tweet, Follow, User timeline, and HomeTimeline cache as distinct pieces.
hints.2: Dual-index the graph; Redis home holds IDs only with a length cap.
hints.3: Tweet DB + author timeline + follower/followee indexes + Redis home:{user} of ~800 IDs + tweet/user caches for hydrate.

phases.goal: Wire async push write path and merge+hydrate read path with the main service boxes.

must_hit.point: Write path: Client → LB → API → Tweet Service (persist + user timeline) → emit tweet.created to MQ → Fan-out workers → Graph Service → if not celebrity, LPUSH/ZADD into each active follower's Redis home.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate draws persist-then-enqueue fan-out workers that push IDs only for non-celebrity active followers.

must_hit.point: Read path: Timeline/Feed Service reads Redis home IDs, fetches recent tweets from celebrity followees' user timelines, merge/sorts by id/time, hydrates tweet+user objects, returns the page.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate merges precomputed home IDs with celebrity pulls, then hydrates before responding.

must_hit.point: Major boxes: API tier, Tweet service, Graph service, Fan-out workers, Timeline service, Redis timeline cluster, Tweet/User DB + caches, object storage + CDN, MQ (Kafka).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate names those services/stores rather than one monolith that does fan-out inline.

probes: Walk the write path for a new tweet and the read path for home timeline.
Which components sit on the critical path of POST /tweets versus GET /feed?

hints.1: Separate the post API from fan-out work and the feed read service.
hints.2: Persist + MQ on write; Redis IDs + celebrity merge + hydrate on read.
hints.3: Tweet service emits to Kafka workers that push non-celebrity homes; feed service merges Redis IDs with celebrity user timelines then hydrates.

phases.goal: Defend hybrid fan-out, async workers, ID caches, celebrity handling, and read-your-writes.

must_hit.point: Hybrid is the expected answer: push for normal accounts; skip push for celebrities above a tunable threshold (~10K–100K historically); at read time merge precomputed timeline + recent celebrity tweets.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate names push + celebrity pull merge and that the threshold is operationally tuned (~10K–100K).

must_hit.point: Never block the post HTTP on millions of Redis writes; use MQ workers with at-least-once delivery and idempotent timeline inserts deduped by tweet_id.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate keeps post latency low via async workers and mentions idempotent/deduped inserts.

must_hit.point: Cache IDs not full content so RAM stays feasible and one tweet object update does not rewrite millions of timelines; hydration is a batch get (watch N+1).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate argues ID-only homes + shared tweet cache, and batch hydration instead of per-ID queries.

must_hit.point: Feed is eventually consistent; give the author read-your-writes by showing their own tweet immediately from user timeline / optimistic UI.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate accepts seconds of follower lag but still surfaces the author's own post right away.

probes: Push vs pull vs hybrid — which do you ship and why?
How do you handle a celebrity tweet without melting fan-out, and how does the author see their own post immediately?

hints.1: Compare write cost of push with read cost of pull.
hints.2: Introduce a follower-count threshold and a read-side merge; keep posting async.
hints.3: Push normals, pull celebrities (~10K–100K threshold), MQ fan-out with tweet_id idempotency, ID cache + hydrate, author read-your-writes from user timeline.

phases.goal: Scale fan-out lag, Redis homes, graph hotspots, hydration, and celebrity delivery p99.

must_hit.point: Fan-out workers / MQ lag: scale consumer groups; shard by author or follower ranges; backpressure + lag alerts; DLQ for poison tweets.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate scales consumers, shards work, and watches lag / DLQ rather than one giant fan-out loop.

must_hit.point: Redis timeline cluster: shard by user_id; replicate; reconstruct on miss from graph + tweet store; do not keep inactive homes forever.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate shards Redis by user_id, plans reconstruction for cold users, and skips eternal inactive homes.

must_hit.point: Graph service hotspots: cache follower lists; paginate huge celebrity follower sets; prefer not materializing full push for celebrities at all.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate treats celebrity follower-list fetch as a bottleneck and leans on pull instead of full push.

must_hit.point: Hydration/tweet store: batch multi-get and tweet cache; CDN for media; avoid joining followers × tweets in one giant SQL at request time.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate hydrates with batched cache/DB gets and rejects a per-refresh SQL join as the read path.

probes: Where does this design break first under load, and how do you scale each hotspot?
What happens when an inactive user returns and their Redis home is missing?

hints.1: Think about fan-out lag, Redis, graph, and hydration separately.
hints.2: Shard Redis by user_id; reconstruct cold homes; pull celebrities instead of full push.
hints.3: Scale MQ consumers with sharding/backpressure/DLQ; Redis shard+replicate+reconstruct; cache/paginate graph; batch hydrate — never SQL JOIN every refresh.

tradeoffs.topic: Push vs pull vs hybrid fan-out
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Push gives O(1)-ish reads but O(followers) writes, celebrity write storms, and inactive waste; pull makes writes cheap but reads slow as follow count grows; hybrid pushes normal accounts, skips celebrities above a tuned threshold (~10K–100K), and merges precomputed home + recent celebrity tweets at read — more complexity (two paths + merge) but the production answer.

Never block the post HTTP on millions of Redis writes; persist then enqueue; workers are at-least-once so timeline inserts must be idempotent (dedupe by tweet_id); user gets fast 200/201 while delivery is eventually consistent.

tradeoffs.topic: Cache full tweet content vs IDs only
tradeoffs.strong_answer: ID-only homes (~800 recent) keep RAM bounded (~15–20 KB/user) and let edits/counts update one tweet object without rewriting millions of timelines; tradeoff is a batch hydration stage that must avoid N+1.

Huge follower-list fetch and fan-out lag (and reply-before-original races) make pure push fail; mitigate by pulling celebrities, prioritizing active followers, and reordering by Snowflake id at serve time; accept higher p99 delivery for huge fanouts.
Home feed is eventually consistent (seconds; p99 worse for huge fanouts); still show the author their own tweet immediately from user timeline / optimistic UI so write UX does not wait on fan-out.

gotchas.trap: Designing only pure push and freezing when asked about Justin Bieber / Lady Gaga.
gotchas.correction: Switch celebrity accounts (above threshold) to pull and merge their recent tweets into the precomputed home at read time.

gotchas.trap: Reply appears in a follower's feed before the original because of long fan-out queues.
gotchas.correction: Sort by Snowflake id at serve time and/or delay reply fan-out until the parent is visible.

gotchas.trap: Assuming unfollow, mute, block, or delete is free after push.
gotchas.correction: Pushed copies go stale; filter at read/hydrate or issue async removals — deletes are fan-out's ugly twin.

gotchas.trap: Keeping push to cold/inactive followers or leaving returnees with an empty Redis home.
gotchas.correction: Skip push while cold; on return, run a reconstruction job from graph + disk tweets into Redis.

gotchas.trap: Proposing SQL JOIN followers × tweets on every home refresh.
gotchas.correction: That dies at read QPS; use it only to motivate precomputed ID timelines.
OFFSET breaks under inserts; use a cursor on tweet_id (Snowflake) or time.

gotchas.trap: Storing full tweet text in every home timeline entry.
gotchas.correction: Causes RAM explosion and painful edits; store IDs and hydrate from tweet/user caches.

gotchas.trap: Conflating search/Trends with the home timeline path.
gotchas.correction: Search is a separate inverted-index path (index on write, scatter-gather on read); mention only if asked.
